overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve its May 31, 2022 minutes, declined to review the draft minutes' sufficiency, and ordered compliance, revised minutes, and member training.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board had not approved minutes of its May 31, 2022 meeting, which remained in draft form and posted online.
allegations.key_passage: As three meetings and 30 days have passed since the May 31, 2022, meeting, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve the minutes of that meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the draft minutes provided were insufficiently detailed to inform the public of what occurred at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: In general, we decline to review the sufficiency of meeting minutes that are still in draft form at the time a complaint is filed.

allegations.summary: The Board did not respond to the complaint within 14 business days, as the AG noted in a preliminary matter; no separate finding was made on this point.
allegations.key_passage: As a preliminary matter, we note that the Board did not respond to the Open Meeting Law complaint.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Revise and approve minutes for the May 31, 2022 meeting consistent with the guidance provided, and certify to the AG within 40 days of the letter.
All current Board members to attend an Open Meeting Law webinar training presented by the AG's office within 90 days of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law, and may result in a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation.
